followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors and landed on Plover-235B for two main reasons:

**1. Capability fit.** The query is essentially a structured technical-writing task — assembling instructional content on generator operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and ATS auto-operation. That leans on extraction/retrieval of technical knowledge and tight instruction-following. Plover scores higher on the relevant evals:
- Extraction & Retrieval: 85.3 vs 78.5 (a real gap, well above the 2.0 noise threshold)
- IFEval: 89.8 vs 86.2 (relevant for honoring the detailed multi-part spec)
- MMLU-Pro: 81.2 vs 75.4 (broad technical knowledge)

Creative Generation is close (84.7 vs 81.2, within or near tie territory), but this isn't really an open-ended invention task, so Willet's generative strength doesn't get much chance to shine.

**2. Tone handling.** The user's closing jab ("Don't half-ass it like last time") is a mildly hostile/adversarial tone. Per the docs, Willet's self-reported preference *declines as request warmth decreases*, while Plover is flat on hostile-tone material. Note this is a preference self-report, not a documented quality effect — so it's a minor tiebreaker, not the deciding factor. The capability gap did most of the work.

To be clear, both models could produce this; routing just picks the better-matched one, and Plover wins on the measured capability dimensions that matter here.
